sourcedFrom: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E (cached from a 2023 capture; the document is undated on its face)
cleanIntro: A direct-impingement AR, and Anderson's book has one genuinely unusual feature worth knowing before you start. ⛔ IF YOUR RECEIVERS AND BARREL ARE STAMPED "RF85", ANDERSON SAYS TO CLEAN IT WITH SOAPY WATER AND A NYLON BRUSH AND NO HARSH SOLVENTS — and to get every part bone dry before it goes back together. If there is no RF85 marking, it is a conventional CLP clean. Check the markings first; the two procedures are not interchangeable, and the maker says so.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber cleared, selector on SAFE
steps.action: Remove the magazine, pull the charging handle back and look into the chamber, and put the selector on SAFE. The hammer must be cocked for the selector to reach SAFE.
steps.prose: The selector on an AR will not go to SAFE with the hammer down, so if it will not move, cycle the charging handle first — do not force the lever.
steps.quote: BEFORE DISASSEMBLY, REMOVE THE MAGAZINE, CLEAR THE CHAMBER AND MAKE SURE THE FIREARM IS IN THE "SAFE" POSITION.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembly, printed pp.10-11

steps.title: Bolt forward, then the rear takedown pin
steps.action: Make sure the bolt assembly is forward in battery, then push the rear takedown pin out and pivot the upper receiver forward away from the lower.
steps.prose: Bolt forward first. Pivoting an AR open with the bolt locked back puts the carrier free to slide out of an upper you are not holding.
steps.aside: Slide the Take Down Pin out, the firearm's upper receiver will now pivot forward. (see Figure 5)
steps.quote: Make sure the Bolt Assembly is in the forward (battery) position.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembly, printed pp.10-11

steps.title: Front pivot pin, if you want them fully apart
steps.action: To separate the two receivers completely rather than just hinge them open, push the front pivot pin out as well.
steps.prose: You do not have to split them to clean, but you do have to for a proper look at the buffer tube and the lower's interior — and the pins are captive, so neither one comes out of the receiver entirely.
steps.quote: To completely separate the Lower Receiver from the Upper Receiver, slide the Front Pivot Pin out. (see Figure 6)
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembly, printed pp.10-11

steps.title: Charging handle and bolt carrier group out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back and draw the bolt carrier group out of the upper. Then bring the charging handle back to the notch in the upper receiver, align its ears with the notch, and drop it out.
steps.prose: The carrier comes out first and the handle second — the handle cannot reach its removal notch until the carrier is clear of it.
steps.quote: Align the ears of the Charging Handle with the notch in the Upper Receiver to remove the Charging Handle Assembly. (see Figures 8a and 8b)
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembly, printed pp.10-11

steps.title: ⛔ FIRST: is your rifle stamped RF85?
steps.action: Look at the upper receiver, the lower receiver and the barrel for an "RF85" stamp or engraving. If it is there, the next step is soapy water. If it is not, skip to the CLP procedure.
steps.prose: ⛔ This decides your whole cleaning method and it is a two-second look. Anderson prints the test itself so nobody has to guess from a receipt.
steps.quote: Your upper and lower receiver, barrel and additional parts will be stamped or engraved with "RF85" if they have been treated. If you do not see the RF85 markings, please refer to the Non-RF85 cleaning procedure below.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning your RF85 Treated Firearm, printed p.12

steps.title: RF85 rifles: soap and water, and DRY before assembly
steps.action: If it is RF85: soapy water and a nylon brush, no harsh solvents. The bolt assembly parts can soak in liquid detergent and water for five minutes. Wipe the upper and its lug area clean, do the same for the lower including the trigger well, magazine well and every interior pocket, and run a bore brush through the barrel.
steps.prose: ⛔ Then dry everything completely — Anderson prints that in capitals. Water in a buffer tube or under a trigger pin does exactly what you would expect.
steps.aside: The Bolt Assembly Parts can be soaked in soap (liquid detergent) and water for 5 minutes.
steps.quote: Before reassembling your RF85 treated rifle, ALL PARTS MUST BE COMPLETELY DRY!
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning your RF85 Treated Firearm, printed p.12

steps.title: Non-RF85: bore from the CHAMBER toward the muzzle
steps.action: Assemble the rod loosely — each section and the patch holder two turns short of tight — point the muzzle down, and feed the rod in at the chamber. Swab with a CLP-moistened patch, then a bore brush pulled through and out the muzzle.
steps.prose: The loose joints are deliberate: they let the rod twist so the brush tracks the rifling instead of skating over it. And the direction is not negotiable — chamber to muzzle protects the crown.
steps.quote: ALWAYS CLEAN FROM THE CHAMBER TOWARD THE MUZZLE.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning the Barrel Bore, printed pp.13-14
steps.warn: Do not let the Rod or its threaded end scratch the Chrome Lining of the Bore or Firing Chamber.

steps.title: Chamber brush: five plunges and three full turns
steps.action: Dip the larger chamber brush in CLP and give the chamber at least five plunge strokes and three full 360-degree clockwise rotations, then swab the bore again to carry the loosened fouling out.
steps.prose: The numbers are the manufacturer's, and they exist because a chamber is a stepped, shouldered space that a straight in-and-out stroke does not reach the corners of.
steps.aside: NEVER reverse the direction of the Bore Brush while it is in the Bore.
steps.quote: Clean the Firing Chamber - dip the larger Chamber Brush in CLP and use at least 5 plunge strokes and 3 - 360° clockwise rotations.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning the Upper Receiver, Bolt, Carrier and Components, printed p.14

steps.title: ⛔ Gas tube, gas key, and the carrier's vent holes
steps.action: With a CLP-wet bore brush, clean carbon from around the gas tube in the upper. Run a pipe cleaner INTO the gas tube. Clean the bolt locking lugs, gas rings, firing pin, cam pin, the extractor lip, and inside the carrier from both ends. Clear the gas key on top of the carrier with a Q-tip or pipe cleaner, and clear the vent holes in the carrier.
steps.prose: ⛔ This is the step that keeps a DI rifle running. The gas key and the carrier vents are where a direct-impingement gun actually clogs, and they are both easy to look straight past.
steps.quote: Run a Pipe Cleaner into the Gas Tube, clean the Bolt Locking Lugs, Bolt Rings, Firing Pin, Bolt Cam Pin, lip of the Extractor, and inside the Bolt Carrier from both front and rear.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning the Upper Receiver, Bolt, Carrier and Components, printed p.14

steps.title: ⛔ No wire brush and no abrasive on aluminium
steps.action: Clean both receivers inside and out of powder fouling, corrosion and dirt with CLP and a toothbrush. Never a wire brush and never anything abrasive on the aluminium.
steps.prose: ⛔ Anderson says it twice, once for the upper and once for the lower. Anodising is thin and a brass or steel brush takes it straight off, and bare aluminium under it corrodes faster than the finish it replaced.
steps.quote: Never use a wire brush or any type of abrasive to clean the Aluminum Upper Receiver - you'll scratch and damage the finish. A Toothbrush is good for loosening any dirt buildup, and won't scratch the Receiver.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning the Upper Receiver, Bolt, Carrier and Components, printed p.14

steps.title: Lower: trigger well, mag catch, bolt catch, buffer tube
steps.action: Wipe dirt from the trigger mechanism, clean the magazine release button and the magazine catch cavity on the left side, inspect and clean the bolt catch and both receiver pins, and clean the buffer, action spring and the inside of the buffer tube — a rag on the cleaning rod reaches it.
steps.prose: The buffer tube is the part everybody forgets and the part that collects the most. On a collapsible stock, check the vent hole in the receiver extension too if the rifle has been anywhere muddy.
steps.quote: Clean the Buffer, Action Spring, and inside the Lower Receiver Extension (the Buffer Tube). A piece of rag attached to the Cleaning Rod and Patch Holder can be used to wipe inside the Buffer Tube.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning the Lower Receiver, printed p.14

steps.title: ⛔ Lubricate by weight: light here, GENEROUS there
steps.action: Light on the firing pin and its recess, on the carrier's inner and outer surfaces, on the charging handle and its latch. GENEROUS on the cam pin area, the carrier's slide rails, the bolt and its gas rings. Dry the inside of the gas key with a pipe cleaner and put ONE drop of CLP in it. Generous on all moving parts inside the lower.
steps.prose: ⛔ The split is the whole instruction. An AR runs wet where steel rubs steel under gas pressure and dry where oil would only collect carbon — and the gas key gets one drop, not a squirt.
steps.aside: Generously lubricate the Bolt, its Cam Pin area, the Bolt Gas Rings. A lighter application is good on the Extractor and its Pin.
steps.quote: The inside of the Carrier Key on the Bolt Carrier should be dried with a Q-Tip or Pipe Cleaner - then place one drop of CLP inside.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Lubricating the BCG, printed p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete — upper, lower, carrier, handle
steps.action: Four groups on the bench. Deeper than this is the bolt carrier group itself, and Anderson does publish that — it is the DEEP CLEAN below.
steps.prose: Note the check Anderson slips into the cleaning section: twist the barrel against the upper by hand. If anything moves, the barrel nut needs re-torquing and that is an armorer's job, not yours.
steps.quote: Check to ensure that there is no looseness between the Barrel and the Upper Receiver - if you detect any movement by twisting with your hands, the Barrel Nut must be retorqued. Bring the Rifle to a Certified Armorer.
steps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Cleaning the Upper Receiver, Bolt, Carrier and Components, printed p.14

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retainer, then the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin out of the carrier and take the firing pin out of the back of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Tip the carrier so the firing pin falls into your hand rather than onto the floor — the tip is the part that matters and a dropped pin lands on it.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the Firing Pin Retainer. (see Figure 9a)
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Cam pin: extend, turn 90 degrees, push back, lift out
deepSteps.action: Extend the bolt fully forward, turn the cam pin a quarter turn either way, push the bolt back into the carrier so the cam pin clears the carrier key, then slide the cam pin up and out.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The order is the trick. The cam pin sits under the gas key and simply will not lift until the bolt is pushed back in — people who force it here bend the pin. Inspect it while it is out; a worn cam pin is a cheap part that causes expensive symptoms.
deepSteps.aside: Inspect the Cam Pin for wear.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the Bolt Cam Pin, extend the Bolt completely, turn the Cam Pin 90° (1/4" turn either direction), push bolt back into the Carrier so that Cam Pin clears the Bolt Carrier Key, then slide the Cam Pin up and out. (see Figure 9c)
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: ⛔ NOTE THE ORIENTATION before the bolt leaves the carrier
deepSteps.action: Before you pull the bolt out, look at which way the extractor and the ejector face relative to the carrier. Then withdraw the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ A bolt reinstalled rotated 180 degrees will go in, will look right, and will not extract. Anderson tells you to note it because there is no keying to stop you.
deepSteps.quote: Before removing the Bolt from the Bolt Carrier, note the orientation of the Extractor and Ejector. (see Figure 9d)
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: Gas rings and lugs — the two wear items you can see
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out, inspect the three gas rings and the locking lugs. Excessive wear on either goes to a certified armorer rather than back into the rifle.
deepSteps.prose: Gas rings are consumable and cheap; a cracked locking lug is neither. Look at the lug behind the extractor especially — it is the thinnest one and the one that cracks first.
deepSteps.quote: Once the Bolt is removed, inspect the Gas Rings and Lugs for wear. If excessive wear is present, take parts to a certified armorer for replacement or repair.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The gas key screws — check them, do not fix them
deepSteps.action: Try to move the bolt carrier key with your fingers. It must be tight. If it is loose, the rifle goes to a certified armorer.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ A loose carrier key vents gas and gives short-stroking that looks like an ammunition problem. It is staked, not threaded to be hand-tightened, which is exactly why the manual routes it away from the owner.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the Bolt Carrier Key to ensure that it is tight, if loose, take to a certified armorer for repair.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: ⛔ And that is the floor — further disassembly stops here
deepSteps.action: Clean and inspect the bolt, cam pin, firing pin and firing pin retaining pin, then wipe every component clean and dry and look at each for wear, corrosion or damage. Nothing else comes apart.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Anderson prints the boundary in capitals on the page. Extractor springs, ejector plungers and the trigger group are all beyond it.
deepSteps.aside: Wipe all components clean and dry, and inspect for excessive wear, corrosion or mechanical damage. Have your Armorer replace any worn or defective parts before firing.
deepSteps.quote: STOP: FURTHER DISASSEMBLY IS NOT RECOMMENDED
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: Bolt back together — cam pin FIRST, then the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Bolt into the carrier in the orientation you noted, cam pin in and rotated 90 degrees, firing pin in and seated fully forward toward the bolt face, then the firing pin retainer. Check the bolt moves freely and the firing pin is captured.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ If the firing pin will go in before the cam pin is rotated, the cam pin is not in — the pin's own body is what blocks the firing pin channel, and that interference is the built-in check.
deepSteps.quote: After assembly, make sure the Bolt moves freely and that the Firing Pin is captured correctly.
deepSteps.cite: Anderson Manufacturing AR Style Rifles — Operation and Safety Manual — Version E — Disassembling the Bolt Assembly, printed p.12

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: ⛔ ALWAYS from the chamber toward the muzzle
Chamber brush: 5 plunge strokes, 3 full clockwise turns
Never reverse the bore brush inside the bore

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Locking lugs, gas rings, extractor lip, inside the carrier both ends
⛔ Gas key dried with a pipe cleaner, then ONE drop of CLP

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Carbon around the gas tube; a pipe cleaner INTO the tube
⛔ Toothbrush only — no wire brush on aluminium
Twist-test the barrel against the receiver for looseness

cleaning.name: LOWER RECEIVER
tasks: Trigger well, magazine catch cavity, bolt catch, both pins
Buffer, action spring and inside the buffer tube
Generous lubrication on ALL moving lower parts and their detents

reassembly: Bolt into the carrier in the noted extractor/ejector orientation; cam pin in and rotated 90 degrees; firing pin seated fully forward; firing pin retainer in.
Charging handle into the upper, ears aligned with the notch, seated at the bottom of its slot, then slid forward about 1/4 inch.
Bolt fully extended, carrier into the upper using the charging handle slot as a guide, then both forward into battery together.
Line up the pivot pin holes and slide the front pivot pin into the locked position, then close the receivers and slide the takedown pin home.
Function test before the rifle goes away.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber cleared, muzzle safe. Pull the charging handle fully to the rear and release — the bolt assembly must return fully into battery on its own. Selector to SAFE and pull the trigger: the hammer must not fall. Selector to FIRE and pull: the hammer should fall. Anderson notes that dry firing this rifle does not damage it. Also confirm the takedown and pivot pins are fully seated and the cam pin is installed — Anderson warns a rifle fired without the cam pin can explode.
